properties.decision:
SETTLED 2026-08-22 BY ANTHONY, IN HIS OWN WORDS: "if the principles are not generally applicable to any design project, then we can discard. I'm just trying to apply some of the things I've learned in developing storyflow to a wider set of projects."

OPTION A IS REJECTED. reflow2 does not ship StoryFlow's nine principles as rules, defaults, or a seeded starter set. They are one project's rules, paid for by one project's incidents, and shipping them would assert that reflow2 knows what a user's engineering standards should be.

THE CRITERION IS GENERAL APPLICABILITY, AND IT IS ALREADY THIS PROJECT'S STANDING RULE. `rule:a-lesson-is-generalised-before-it-is-built` says it from his words of 2026-08-14: "I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable." A principle is carried in only if the GENERAL form is true of any design project; the specific form that produced it stays in StoryFlow.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN. It does not mean the nine were unhelpful — the opposite. They are field evidence from a real deployment, and two of them (rules A and B) name failure modes reflow2 both practises and violates. The ruling is about what SHIPS, not about what is worth reading.

THE SORT ITSELF IS A SEPARATE ACT and is not settled here. Which of the nine have a general form, which are already carried by existing reflow2 vocabulary, and which are code-level lints over a user's source that reflow2 must not attempt, is the follow-on question. The sibling ideas hold the three that survived a first pass.

⭐ ONE MEASURED FINDING SURVIVES REGARDLESS OF THE SORT, because it is about reflow2 rather than about StoryFlow: principle B ("a set reduced to a scalar is not a check of the set") is VIOLATED BY REFLOW2'S OWN INSTRUMENT. `vocabulary_coverage` counts unused properties in `properties_on_used_types` and its `unused` list names node types and edge types only — so an unused PROPERTY is counted and never named, and no report can say WHICH vocabulary a design has never touched. Found 2026-08-22 by asserting the opposite in a test and watching it fail.
properties.name: DECIDED — a StoryFlow principle enters reflow2 only in its GENERAL form; what is not generally applicable to any design project is discarded
properties.no_relation_note: Searched 2026-08-22 for existing nodes on reflow2 serving other projects vs itself. Nearest were rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party — both READ and judged NOT related in the relation vocabulary's sense. They state the PRINCIPLE that reflow2 serves other projects; this asks a narrower product question those rules do not reach, namely whether reflow2 may ship another project's engineering standards as content. A DEPENDS_ON would be false (this is answerable without either rule) and a CONTRADICTS would be false (option C is compatible with both). Recorded as a note rather than a forced edge: a false neighbour would put those two rules in front of every later reader of this question and they do not answer it. NOTE WRITTEN BY HAND because review_relations was not on this session's served tool surface — the server was rebuilt mid-session and the client's tool list is fixed at connect time.
properties.rationale: Recorded as decided rather than left open because Anthony stated the criterion directly and it matches a standing rule he had already given. Option A is closed by his word. What remains is the per-principle sort, which is work rather than a decision, and the one product finding above, which stands on its own measurement.
